the study of the effect of integrated management of nutrients on the yield of onion (A. cepa L. in North Gujarat.
the effect of integrated nutrients management on economics of Onion.
the effects of integrated nutrient management in onion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
integrated nutrient management with vermicompost (75% RDN) was found to be the best among the treatments evaluated for onion production under north Gujarat conditions.

the application of vermicompost (100%) + 25% N (through chemical fertilizer) was found most effective in terms of growth and yield attributes and it was found to be the most economic and eco-friendly treatment.
the treatment T7 (75% RDN 25% N) through vermicomposts was found to be the most promising treatment for maximum bulb yield and net return in onion crop under north Gujarat conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the application of 75% RND through vermicomposting and 25% through chemical fertilizers (NPK) was found to be best for maximum bulb yield and economic returns.
the treatment T7 (75% RDN (100: 50: 50) kg/ha through vermicompos and 25% N as urea through chemical fertilizer) recorded significantly highest bulb yield and maximum net returns and B: C ratio.
integrated nutrient management with vermicompost and poultry manure recorded the highest bulb yield and marketable bulb yield.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the integrated nutrient management with vermicompost (75% RDN + 25% N) is the best option for onion production in north Gujarat.
vermicompost, neem cake, and poultry manure are good sources of nutrients for onion cultivation.
the application of 75% RND through vermicomposts 25% N as chemical fertilizer was found to be the best treatment for onion cultivation.
